analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds one paragraph at docs/architecture/hardware-support.md lines 351-356 and one failure-mode table row at docs/architecture/inference.md line 2371. Both describe an Autopilot placement hold: an unexpired hold removes a slot from eviction snapshots (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots) and denies its weights any free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes). A load that would need to evict a held slot is refused with the ordinary slot or insufficient-memory error.

Security relevance: this is a local availability and memory-admission behaviour. It touches T-029 (a resident model monopolising the GPU) and TB-007 only indirectly. The text does not alter any control in the threat model: no attestation, encryption, App Attest authorization, coordinator wire contract, prefix-cache storage, or key handling is changed. The prefix-cache threat T-041, which was supplied as relevant, is unaffected.

The remaining hardware-support.md content in the supplied units is unchanged context and not part of the PR diff. I did not re-audit it for pre-existing issues.

Unverified contract: the Swift implementation (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift), the hold's expiry bound and the hold's authorization source (coordinator-driven or local) are not in the supplied evidence. A reviewer of the code change should confirm that the hold is time-bounded and cannot be set by an untrusted party to starve other model loads, a DoS concern under ADV-001/ADV-002/T-029. The inference.md unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:0 has metadata only and no body, so the patch in unit :1 was the only evidence for that file. I identified no regression from the docs alone.
